title: Reservoir computing with error correction: Long-term behaviors of stochastic dynamical systems
reason_a: 'Traditional Reservoir Computing' (contrasted with the added Normalizing Flow error model) -> term of art for the standard random recurrent network with internal state -> steps 1-3 resolve to F1, default F1.1. Flagged judgement: inference from terminology rather than an explicit mechanism statement; unassignable was the considered alternative.
reason_b: Only 'Reservoir Computing' is named; 'traditional Reservoir Computing' contrasts with the proposed Normalizing-Flow-augmented variant, not with a specific architecture. State-generation mechanism (F1 recurrent network vs F3 feature map) undetermined from title+abstract.
deciding_text: The only architectural statement in the abstract is: "we propose a data-driven framework combining Reservoir Computing and Normalizing Flow to study this issue, which mimics error modeling to improve traditional Reservoir Computing performance". The word "recurrent" does not occur anywhere in the title or abstract, and no network, delay loop, feature window or medium is described. "Traditional Reservoir Computing" is contrastive with the authors' own Normalizing-Flow-augmented variant, not with a named architecture. Decisively: an NG-RC (F3) paper describes itself against "traditional reservoir computing" in the same words, so the phrase does not discriminate F1 from F3 and cannot carry the step 1-3 cascade.
reconciled_rule: [Joint record. Coder A draft 2026-09-05; read against the abstracts and countersigned by Coder B 2026-09-05.] Resolved to unassignable. Coder B's call adopted; Coder A's F1.1 withdrawn. Coder A's assignment rested on "traditional Reservoir Computing" being a term of art for a random recurrent network, which is inference from convention and is forbidden by codebook 0.1: code what the paper reports, not what it implies or what you infer is standard; widespread convention is not a substitute for a stated value. Candidate section 11 ruling: a bare "reservoir computing" or "traditional reservoir computing", with no stated state-generation mechanism, is unassignable and never F1 by default. Nomenclature alone never decides a family, on the same grounds that substrate alone never does. Unassignable reason category: abstract names reservoir computing but does not describe the state-generating system. Consistent with both coders' independent calls on RC-6308 and RC-5868. Note for the pilot-design decision: this record would survive an eligibility screen, so it is a genuine source-uninformative case rather than a screening artefact. COUNTERSIGN, Coder B, 2026-09-05: agreed, the resolution stands and my unassignable call is the joint call. Deciding text checked against the abstract itself: the quoted sentence is verbatim; "recurrent" occurs nowhere in the title or abstract, and neither does "network". One precision note that changes nothing in the resolution: "delay" does occur once, in "stochastic delay differential equations", which names a class of target system being predicted and not a reservoir delay loop. The deciding text's "no network, delay loop, feature window or medium is described" is therefore exact as written, and a later reader grepping for "delay" alone should not read it as contradicted. I also confirm the eligibility observation the rule rests on: this is a primary research article reporting quantitative results on three named test systems, so it survives an eligibility screen and is still unassignable. That is what makes it evidence for the pilot-design decision rather than a screening artefact, and it is the half of the pair that option (b) would not remove.
